mainTopic: Twilight, signs for the start of שבת, and the שופר blasts on ערב שבת
overview: This amud first finishes the earlier discussion of רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי on בין השמשות: for eating תרומה we follow רבי יוסי's later twilight. שמואל then gives a star-count rule: one star means day, two means בין השמשות, and three means night. A ברייתא supports this rule, and רבי יוסי adds that only medium-sized stars count. רבי יוסי ברבי זבידא shows that a person who does מלאכה during both twilights of שבת is חייב חטאת either way. רבא gives his servant simple signs for when to light the candles, including signs from nature for a cloudy day. Two ברייתות describe the six שופר blasts sounded on ערב שבת, and the גמרא discusses the Babylonian custom and corrects רב יהודה's teaching to follow רבי נתן. רבי יוסי בר חנינא's claim that one may still light after the six blasts is rejected, because the חזן simply left his שופר on his roof. This leads to a question about whether a שופר may be moved on שבת, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's twilight applies to eating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'we follow רבי יוסי for תרומה' refers to when כהנים may eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ruling refers to eating תרומה: כהנים do not eat תרומה until רבי יוסי's בין השמשות has fully ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering an earlier question about what 'we follow רבי יוסי for תרומה' means. The answer is that it refers to the time when a כהן may eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, בין השמשות starts and ends later than it does according to רבי יהודה. A כהן who became impure must wait until it is truly night before eating תרומה. So waiting until the end of רבי יוסי's later twilight is the stricter choice, just as following רבי יהודה's earlier twilight is the stricter choice for starting שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Eating תרומה, the portion of produce given to a כהן
Twilight, the doubtful period between day and night

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the הלכה can follow different תנאים for different issues, choosing the stricter view each time.

phrases.english: Rather, it refers to eating terumah,
phrases.notes: This answers a question from the previous lines, which asked what 'for תרומה' means.

phrases.english: that priests do not eat terumah

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּשָׁלֵים בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: until the twilight of Rabbi Yosei is completed.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי's twilight is very short and comes after רבי יהודה's twilight has ended.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question earlier about what 'for תרומה' means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining which law the ruling refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might have thought the ruling refers to some other law involving תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling refers to the time when a כהן may eat תרומה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We follow רבי יהודה for שבת and רבי יוסי for eating תרומה, which is the stricter view in each case.

steps.title: שמואל's star-count rule for day, twilight, and night
steps.stepSummary: שמואל defines day, בין השמשות, and night by how many stars can be seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: one star means it is still day, two stars means it is בין השמשות, and three stars means it is night.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a simple way to tell the time in the evening: count the stars in the sky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion measured twilight in abstract terms. שמואל gives a practical sign that anyone can see. The second star marks the start of בין השמשות, and the third star marks the start of night.
steps.whatToRemember: One star means day, two means בין השמשות, and three means night.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
one star — it is day,
two — it is twilight,
three — it is night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the dispute about twilight to a practical way of measuring it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The number of visible stars determines day (one), בין השמשות (two), and night (three).

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same star rule
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports שמואל with the same wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: one star means day, two means בין השמשות, and three means night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up שמואל by quoting a ברייתא that says exactly the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל is an אמורא, and a teaching from the time of the תנאים carries more weight. Quoting the ברייתא shows that שמואל's rule is an older, established teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (introduces a supporting ברייתא)

phrases.english: It was also taught so in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹכָב אֶחָד יוֹם, שְׁנַיִם בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת,
phrases.english: one star — day; two — twilight;
three — night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording

steps.title: Only medium-sized stars count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי, within the ברייתא, explains which kind of stars count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: this does not mean the large stars that can be seen even by day, or the small stars that appear only late at night. It means the medium-sized stars.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues, and רבי יוסי explains which stars the rule is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Large stars show up while it is still light, so counting them would declare night too early. Tiny stars appear only when it is already fully dark, so counting them would declare night too late. Only medium stars give the correct measure.
steps.confusionAlert: This רבי יוסי is the תנא quoted inside the ברייתא. He is not רבי יוסי ברבי זבידא, the אמורא in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
phrases.notes: This is still part of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: not large stars that are seen by day,
and not small stars
that are seen only at night —
but rather medium ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the star rule from steps 2 and 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The star count refers to medium-sized stars.

steps.title: Work during both twilights makes one liable either way
steps.stepSummary: Someone who does מלאכה during both the Friday and the Saturday-night בין השמשות is definitely חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי זבידא said: a person who does forbidden work during both twilights of שבת is obligated to bring a חטאת, whichever way you look at it.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא points out that the doubt about בין השמשות can be settled if someone worked during both twilights of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בין השמשות counts as night, then Friday's twilight was already שבת. If it counts as day, then Saturday night's twilight was still שבת. Either way, one of the two acts was done on שבת, so the person is surely obligated to bring a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offering brought for an accidental transgression

steps.whyThisMatters: A single act during בין השמשות is a doubt and cannot require a חטאת. Two acts during the two twilights turn that doubt into certainty.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Zevida said:
one who does labor during two twilights —
phrases.notes: The twilight that begins שבת and the twilight that ends it.

phrases.english: is liable to a sin-offering whichever way you take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the doubtful status of בין השמשות to a case of liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work done during both twilights of שבת creates a certain obligation to bring a חטאת.

steps.title: רבא's simple sign for lighting שבת candles
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells his servant to light the candles while the sun is still on the tops of the palm trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to his servant: you are not expert in the Rabbis' measurements, so light the lamp while the sun is still on the tops of the palm trees.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a simple everyday sign for someone who cannot calculate בין השמשות exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exact measurements are hard for ordinary people to apply. When sunlight is visible only on the treetops, sunset is close but has not yet happened. Lighting then is safely before שבת begins.

keyTerms.meaning: You are expert in, you know clearly

phrases.english: Rava said to his servant:
You, who are not expert
in the measure of the Sages,
while the sun is on top of the palm trees,
light the lamp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from theory to practical guidance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Light the candles when the sun is still on the treetops.

steps.title: What to do on a cloudy day
steps.stepSummary: The question is asked: what sign should be used when the sun cannot be seen?
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a cloudy day?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question: רבא's sign does not work when clouds hide the sun, so another sign is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question does not attack רבא's sign. It simply asks for a backup sign for a situation where the first one cannot be used.

phrases.english: On a cloudy day, what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case where step 6's sign cannot be used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A sign for the approach of evening when the sun is hidden.

steps.title: Roosters, ravens, or plants as evening signs
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: in the city, watch the roosters; in the field, watch the ravens or the אדאני plants.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the city, watch the roosters. In the field, watch the ravens, or alternatively the אדאני plants.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives signs from nature that show evening is coming, even without seeing the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roosters go up to their perches toward evening, and ravens return to their nests. The אדאני plants turn toward the west in the evening. Each of these acts like a natural clock.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of plant that turns westward in the evening

steps.whatToRemember: When the exact time cannot be calculated, natural signs can show that שבת is approaching.

phrases.english: In the city — watch the rooster.
In the field — the ravens,
or alternatively — the adanei plants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The behavior of roosters, ravens, or אדאני plants shows that evening is coming.

steps.title: Six שופר blasts on ערב שבת: the first two
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that six blasts are sounded on ערב שבת: the first stops field work, and the second closes the city and its stores.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: six blasts are sounded on ערב שבת. The first stops the people from working in the fields. The second stops work in the city and closes the stores.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא describes the public system of שופר blasts that warned everyone that שבת was coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blasts come in stages. Field workers are far from home, so they are warned first. City workers and shopkeepers are warned next.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
They sound six blasts on Shabbat eve.
The first — to stop the people
from work in the fields.
The second — to stop the city and the stores.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן שֵׁשׁ תְּקִיעוֹת תּוֹקְעִין עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of practical signals for the start of שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six blasts are sounded on ערב שבת, and the first two stop work in the fields and in the city.

steps.title: What the third blast is for: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says the third blast signals lighting the candles. רבי יהודה הנשיא says it signals removing תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The third blast is for lighting the candle, according to רבי נתן. רבי יהודה הנשיא says: the third blast is for removing תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא records a disagreement about what the third blast signals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the third blast marks the last tasks before שבת. They differ only about which task it announces: lighting candles or taking off תפילין, which are not worn on שבת.

phrases.english: The third — to light the lamp,
these are the words of Rabbi Natan.
Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:
The third — to remove phylacteries.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלִישִׁית לְהַדְלִיק אֶת הַנֵּר דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the third blast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether the third blast signals lighting candles or removing תפילין.

steps.title: A short pause, then the final blasts and שבת begins
steps.stepSummary: After the third blast he waits briefly, then sounds תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה, and stops all work.
steps.simpleTranslation: He waits about as long as it takes to roast a small fish or to stick bread onto the oven wall. Then he sounds a תקיעה, a תרועה, and a תקיעה, and rests.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes: after a short pause, the last three blasts are sounded and שבת begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pause gives a forgetful person a last moment for quick food preparation. The final three blasts complete the six, and then the one blowing the שופר also stops working.

keyTerms.meaning: To stick bread dough onto the oven wall

steps.whatToRemember: Six blasts: the first stops field work, the second closes the city, the third is for candles or תפילין, then a short pause, then תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה, and שבת begins.

phrases.english: And he waits as long as roasting a small fish
or sticking bread in the oven,
and he sounds a tekia, a terua, and a tekia, and rests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the six-blast sequence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a short pause, the final תקיעה, תרועה, and תקיעה are sounded and שבת begins.

steps.title: The Babylonian blast custom
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל describes how the Babylonians blow before שבת: a תקיעה and a תרועה, and they stop working during the תרועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: What can we do about the Babylonians? They blow a תקיעה and a תרועה, and they begin resting during the תרועה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reports a different custom that the Babylonian Jews follow for the last blasts before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 taught that the final set is תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה, and only then does one stop working. The Babylonians stop earlier, during the תרועה, without waiting for a final תקיעה.

keyTerms.meaning: They sound a תרועה (the broken, wavering blast)
They stop working and accept שבת

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
What shall we do with the Babylonians,
who sound a tekia and sound a terua
and stop working during the terua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: מַה נַּעֲשֶׂה לָהֶם לַבַּבְלִיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a different local custom alongside the ברייתא's order of blasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Babylonians blow a תקיעה and a תרועה and accept שבת during the תרועה.

steps.title: That only adds up to five blasts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording: a תקיעה and a תרועה would make only five blasts in total, not six.
steps.simpleTranslation: They blow only a תקיעה and a תרועה? Then there are only five blasts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that six blasts are sounded on ערב שבת. Three blasts come first, and adding just a תקיעה and a תרועה gives only five. So the wording as quoted cannot be correct.

phrases.english: They sound a tekia and a terua?
That makes only five!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The quoted wording of the Babylonian custom
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A total of six blasts is fixed. Three earlier blasts plus a תקיעה and a תרועה only add up to five.

steps.title: Corrected version of the Babylonian custom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the text: the Babylonians blow תקיעה, another תקיעה, then a תרועה, and stop during the תרועה. They are following their fathers' custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: they blow a תקיעה, blow a תקיעה again, then blow a תרועה, and stop working during the תרועה. They hold on to the custom of their fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by fixing the wording so that the total comes to six blasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two תקיעות before the תרועה, the count becomes six. The difference from step 11 is the order: the Babylonians end with the תרועה instead of a תקיעה. The words מנהג אבותיהן בידיהן explain that they keep doing this because it is their inherited custom.

keyTerms.meaning: In their hands, meaning they hold on to it

steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is not saying the Babylonians blow fewer blasts. They also blow six. Only the ORDER of the last three blasts is different.

phrases.english: Rather: they sound a tekia, and again sound a tekia,
and sound a terua, and stop working during the terua.
The custom of their fathers is in their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 13 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Babylonians blow just a תקיעה and a תרועה, which would make five blasts.
steps.terutzMaskana: They blow תקיעה, תקיעה, תרועה, which makes six, and they stop during the תרועה because of their fathers' custom.

steps.title: רב יהודה teaches that the second blast is for lighting
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה taught his son רב יצחק that the second blast signals lighting the נר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה taught his son רב יצחק: the second blast is to light the candle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a teaching that רב יהודה gave his son about which blast signals lighting the שבת candles. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 brought two views about the third blast. Here רב יהודה seems to put candle lighting at the second blast, which does not obviously match either view.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda taught Rav Yitzchak his son:
The second blast is to light the candle.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new teaching that touches on the dispute of step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As quoted, the second blast signals lighting the נר.

steps.title: This matches neither רבי נתן nor רבי יהודה הנשיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view this follows. It fits neither רבי נתן (third blast is for lighting) nor רבי יהודה הנשיא (third blast is for removing תפילין).
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is not like רבי נתן, and not like רבי יהודה הנשיא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's teaching because it does not fit any known opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי נתן and רבי יהודה הנשיא agree that the second blast closes the city and its stores. They only argue about the third blast. So nobody holds that lighting happens at the second blast.

phrases.english: According to whom?

phrases.aramaic: לָא כְּרַבִּי נָתָן, וְלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא!
phrases.english: Not like Rabbi Natan, and not like Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? לָא כְּרַבִּי נָתָן, וְלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the teaching of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's statement that the second blast is for lighting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions in the ברייתא give the second blast to closing the stores. Neither puts lighting there.

steps.title: Correction: the third blast is for lighting, like רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the teaching to 'the third blast is to light the candle,' which follows רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he taught: the third blast is to light the candle. Whose view is that? רבי נתן's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רב יהודה's teaching so that it matches a known opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the text is changed from 'second' to 'third,' the teaching fits רבי נתן exactly. This also shows that רב יהודה ruled like רבי נתן.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב יהודה held like רבי נתן that the third blast is the signal to light the שבת candles.

phrases.english: Rather: the third blast is to light the candle.
According to whom? According to Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה taught that the second blast is for lighting.
steps.terutzMaskana: He taught that the third blast is for lighting, following רבי נתן.

steps.title: דבי רבי ישמעאל: the first blast ends field work
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that six blasts are sounded. At the first blast, field workers stop working, and they all enter the city together. The stores are still open.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: six blasts are sounded on ערב שבת. When he starts the first blast, the people in the fields stop hoeing, plowing, and all field work. Those working close to the city may not go in until those working far away arrive, so that everyone enters together. At this point the stores are still open and the shutters are still in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, more detailed ברייתא that describes what happens at each blast, starting with the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds details that the earlier ברייתא did not give. The nearby workers must wait so that people will not suspect the late arrivals of working after the blast. City life, like the open stores, still goes on at this stage.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
Those who are near / those who are far
Shop shutters, used as stands to display goods

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Six blasts are sounded on Shabbat eve.
When he began to sound the first blast,
those standing in the field refrained
from hoeing and from plowing
and from doing any work of the fields.
And those who are near may not enter
until those who are far arrive,
and they all enter together.
And still the stores are open and the shutters are in place.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: שֵׁשׁ תְּקִיעוֹת תּוֹקְעִין עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel, more detailed ברייתא on the same six blasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first blast stops all field work, and the workers enter the city together.

steps.title: The second blast closes the stores
steps.stepSummary: At the second blast the shutters are removed and the stores are locked, but the food is still sitting on the stove.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he starts the second blast, the shutters are taken away and the stores are locked. But hot water and pots are still sitting on the stove.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with what happens at the second blast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Business in the city now stops completely. Home preparations are not finished yet, because the food is still cooking on the כירה.

phrases.english: When he began to sound the second blast,
the shutters were removed and the stores were locked,

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲדַיִין חַמִּין מוּנָּחִין עַל גַּבֵּי כִּירָה
phrases.english: and still hot water is sitting on the stove
and pots are sitting on the stove.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second blast closes the stores, while the food may still stay on the stove.

steps.title: The third blast and the final set
steps.stepSummary: At the third blast the food is removed, the hot food is insulated, and the candles are lit. After a short pause he blows תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה and stops.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he starts the third blast, whoever is removing food removes it, whoever is insulating food insulates it, and whoever is lighting lights. He waits about as long as it takes to fry a small fish or to stick bread onto the oven wall. Then he blows a תקיעה, a תרועה, and a תקיעה, and stops working.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by describing the third blast and the final three blasts that begin שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third blast is the time for the last home preparations, including lighting, which matches רבי נתן. The short pause gives people a few final moments. After that come the closing three blasts, and then שבת begins.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who removes (food from the stove) removed it
The one who insulates (hot food) insulated it
Roasting a small fish, used as a short measure of time
To stick bread onto the wall of the oven

steps.whatToRemember: Order of the six blasts: 1) field work stops; 2) stores close; 3) remove food, insulate it, and light; then a short pause; 4-6) תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה, and שבת begins.

phrases.english: When he began to sound the third blast,
the one removing removed, and the one insulating insulated,
and the one lighting lit.
And he waits as long as it takes to roast a small fish,
or to stick bread onto the oven,
and he sounds a tekia, a terua, and a tekia, and stops working.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third blast is for removing food, insulating it, and lighting. After a short pause, the final three blasts begin שבת.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר חנינא: one may still light after six blasts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא heard that someone who comes to light after all six blasts may still light.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: I heard that if someone comes to light after the six blasts, he may light.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא adds a ruling: even right after the sixth blast, שבת has not quite begun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that שבת starts exactly at the last blast. רבי יוסי בר חנינא says there is still a small window of time for lighting afterward.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
I heard that if one comes to light
after six blasts, he may light.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: שָׁמַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ruling about the time just after the final blast described in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may still light the candles after the six blasts.

steps.title: Proof: the חזן had time to bring his שופר home
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא proves his point: the חכמים gave the חזן הכנסת time to carry his שופר home after blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the חכמים gave the synagogue attendant a set amount of time to take his שופר home.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא backs up his ruling with a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying the שופר home is not allowed on שבת. If the חזן was given time to do it after the last blast, then שבת must not have begun yet. So lighting is also still allowed during that time.

keyTerms.meaning: The synagogue attendant who blew the blasts

phrases.english: For the Sages gave a set time
to the synagogue attendant to take his shofar to his house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling of step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That lighting is allowed after the six blasts
steps.raayaSupportSource: The time the חכמים gave the חזן הכנסת to bring his שופר home

steps.title: Objection: that would make the time different for everyone
steps.stepSummary: The others reply that if this were true, the start of שבת would depend on how far each חזן lives, so the measure would change from place to place.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If so, you have made your ruling depend on varying amounts of time.
steps.whatsHappening: The other scholars reject רבי יוסי בר חנינא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every חזן lives at a different distance from where he blows. If שבת began only after he reached home, there would be no fixed time for שבת. That cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: You have made your words depend on varying measures

phrases.english: They said to him: If so,
you have made your words depend on varying measures.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אִם כֵּן נָתַתָּ דְּבָרֶיךָ לְשִׁיעוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the חזן bringing his שופר home
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the start of שבת depend on each חזן's distance from home, so there would be no uniform time.

steps.title: The חזן hid his שופר on his roof
steps.stepSummary: The real explanation: the חזן had a hidden spot on top of his roof, where he left the שופר, because a שופר and trumpets may not be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the synagogue attendant had a hidden place on top of his roof, and there he put down his שופר. This is because neither a שופר nor trumpets may be moved on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The others explain what the 'set time' for the חזן really was, which removes רבי יוסי בר חנינא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חזן did not carry the שופר home at all. He put it down right where he was, so no extra time was needed and שבת could begin right after the last blast. The reason he had to put it down there is that a שופר and trumpets are מוקצה and may not be moved on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: The others hold that there is no extra time after the six blasts: שבת begins right away. The חזן's 'set time' was only to put the שופר down on his roof, because a שופר is מוקצה.

phrases.english: Rather, there is a hidden place
for the synagogue attendant on top of his roof,
where he puts down his shofar.
Because one may not move

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַשּׁוֹפָר וְלֹא אֶת הַחֲצוֹצְרוֹת.
phrases.english: neither the shofar nor the trumpets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מָקוֹם צָנוּעַ יֵשׁ לוֹ לְחַזַּן הַכְּנֶסֶת בְּרֹאשׁ גַּגּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection of step 23 by giving a different reading of the חזן's 'set time.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חזן was given time to carry his שופר home, so שבת starts later and one may light after the six blasts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חזן put the שופר down in a hidden spot on his roof, so no extra time was needed and שבת begins right after the blasts.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A שופר and trumpets may not be moved on שבת, and the time given to the חזן does not prove that there is extra time to light.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי יוסי בר חנינא's proof (step 22) that the חזן was given time to carry his שופר home
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'set time' was only for putting the שופר down in a hidden spot on the roof, not for walking home. So it does not show any extra time after the six blasts, and שבת begins immediately.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a שופר may be moved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 24 with a ברייתא that says a שופר may be moved on שבת, though חצוצרות may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: a שופר may be moved on שבת, but trumpets may not be moved!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions what it just said in Step 24. A ברייתא seems to say the opposite: a שופר may be moved on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 put the שופר and the חצוצרות in the same group: neither may be moved on שבת. This ברייתא separates them. The trumpets still may not be moved, but the שופר may. So the question is about the שופר only.

keyTerms.meaning: May be moved or carried around (on שבת)

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody disagrees about the trumpets. Both sources say they may not be moved. The whole question is only about the שופר.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: a shofar may be moved
phrases.notes: Contradicts Step 24, which said a שופר may not be moved.

phrases.english: and trumpets may not be moved!
phrases.notes: On trumpets, the ברייתא agrees with Step 24.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 24, that a שופר may not be moved on שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement in Step 24 that a שופר may not be moved on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says outright that a שופר may be moved, which contradicts Step 24.

steps.title: An individual's שופר versus a community's שופר
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the ברייתא is about a private person's שופר, while Step 24 is about a community's שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is not a problem. Here (the ברייתא that allows moving it) is about an individual's שופר. There (the rule that forbids it) is about a community's שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף shows that both sources are correct. Each one is talking about a different שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A private person's שופר may be moved. A community's שופר may not. The שופר in Step 24 belonged to the community, since the חזן הכנסת blew it for the whole town, so it may not be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a problem (the start of an answer)
Here... there (each source is about a different case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the same object can follow different rules on שבת. It depends on who owns it and how it is normally used.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: it is not difficult:
phrases.notes: Some versions say רב יוסי, the name in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is רב יוסף.

phrases.english: here, regarding an individual,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא that allows moving it is about a privately owned שופר.

phrases.english: there, regarding a community.
phrases.notes: Step 24 is about the community's שופר, the one the חזן used.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּיָחִיד, כָּאן בְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is about a different situation (individual versus community).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources were thought to be talking about every שופר, so they seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: An individual's שופר may be moved. A community's שופר may not.

steps.title: What use does a private שופר have on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks what permitted use an individual's שופר has on שבת that would allow moving it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: And an individual's שופר, what is it good for (on שבת)?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks רב יוסף to explain his answer. A שופר may not be blown on שבת, so what could a private person use it for that day?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object may only be moved on שבת if it has some use that is allowed on שבת. Blowing a שופר is not allowed. So אביי wants to know what other use makes an individual's שופר different. He is not rejecting the answer. He is asking for the reason behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it fit for? What use does it have?

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: אביי is speaking to רב יוסף, who was his teacher.

phrases.english: And with an individual, for what is it fit?
phrases.notes: He asks what permitted use it has on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּבְיָחִיד לְמַאי חֲזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the answer in Step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What permitted use makes an individual's שופר allowed to move on שבת.

steps.title: A שופר can be used to give water
steps.stepSummary: An individual's שופר may be moved because it can be used to give someone a drink of water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is fit to give water with it.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the answer to אביי's question. A private שופר has a use that is allowed on שבת: it can be used to give someone water to drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A horn is hollow, so it can hold water and be used to give someone a drink. That use is allowed on שבת, so on this answer an individual's שופר is not מוקצה and may be moved. The amud ends here. The גמרא continues on the next amud and questions whether this use really sets the individual's שופר apart from the community's.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is fit (for some use)
To give someone a drink, to let them sip

steps.whatToRemember: On רב יוסף's distinction, an individual's שופר may be moved on שבת because it can be used to give water. The discussion of whether this really separates it from a community's שופר continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: since it is fit to give water to drink with it.
phrases.notes: This permitted use is what lets it be moved on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question in Step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An individual's שופר can be used to give water, which is allowed on שבת, so it may be moved.
